newsitem.title: USA: Grand Union posts huge loss; cuts headquarters jobs.
newsitem.headline: Grand Union posts huge loss; cuts headquarters jobs.

text.p: The Grand Union Co. Thursday reported a loss of more than $78 million in the latest quarter and the struggling supermarket chain, whose president resigned earlier this month, said it was cutting 80 jobs at its corporate headquarters.
Grand Union said it lost $78.2 million, or $7.82 a share, in its fiscal fourth quarter ended March 29, compared with a year-ago loss of $29.2 million, or $2.93 a share.
Revenues slipped to $515.2 million from $519.9 million.

The company, which has 226 stores in New Jersey, New York, New Hampshire, Connecticut, Pennsylvania and Vermont, said it took a pre-tax charge of $9.8 million in the fourth quarter, which included $7.8 million in connection with its reorganization.
It said the lay-offs and division consolidations are expected to save more than $5 million.
"We sincerely regret the necessity of laying off such a large number of valued Grand Union associates," said interim Chief Executive Officer Roger Stangeland.
He said the reorganization will affect all areas of the company.
"The reorganization was implemented to benefit all of our constituencies: customers, shareholders and the remaining 15,000 associates," Stangeland said.
The company said it is conducting a search for a new president and chief executive officer to replace Joseph J. McCaig, who resigned on May 7.
Grand Union's stock was off 37.5 cents at $2 in early trading on the Nasdaq market.
